newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says last Hebron hurdles can be quickly solved.
newsitem.headline: PLO says last Hebron hurdles can be quickly solved.

text.p: Senior PLO officials said on Tuesday that Israeli and Palestinian peace teams could quickly resolve remaining issues barring a deal on a long-overdue Israeli redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
"The remaining issues are very silly. They could be overcome very quickly," Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's adviser Nabil Abu Rdaineh told Reuters.
"If the Israelis have the political decision to resolve them today, the agreement would be signed today," he said.

Israeli and Palestine Liberation Organisation peace teams ended a round of talks early on Tuesday at the home of U.S. Consul-General Edward Abington. The sides were rushed from a Jerusalem hotel after a bomb scare late on Monday.

"We have four problems that need to be resolved before we can conclude the drafting which we hope will be done today," chief PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat told Reuters without elaborating. "We will review today and try to finish."

Erekat said the sides were due to return to the negotiating table later on Tuesday. He said on Monday the teams were putting the final touches on the long-elusive Hebron deal ahead of a signing by Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai was also optimistic a deal was at hand. "I predict this accord will be signed tomorrow (Tuesday)," he said on Monday.

At least seven right-wing ministers in Netanyahu's 18-member cabinet were expected to oppose the deal. Jewish settlers warned the handover would lead to bloodshed in the town holy to Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.

A recent breakthrough in the talks came during a lightning mediation mission by Jordan's King Hussein on Sunday. The king nudged the sides to accept a timetable for three further Israeli troop pullbacks from rural West Bank areas.
A 1995 peace deal committed Israel to complete the further redeployments by September 1997. The sides agreed to a compromise date of mid-1998.

Hebron is the last of seven Israeli-occupied West Bank towns due to be given Palestinian rule under the 1995 peace deal. It is the only one of the seven where Jews live in the heart of an Arab population. Netanyahu has sought to bolster security arrangements for the 400 Jewish settlers in the heart of the city of 100,000 Arabs.
The town was due to be handed over to the Palestinians last March but violence, security concerns and Israel's change of government in June have delayed the pullback.
